rationale: This headline economic-magnitude summary follows directly from the reproduced fully-controlled 2SLS coefficients scaled by the 2000-2007 interquartile exposure differential. The differential is 1.060 = (p75 3.1138 - p25 1.5994 = 1.5145) x 0.7, from outputs/apptab1_importgrowth.csv (year 2000), matching the ~$1,060/worker specified. Applying it: (1) manufacturing employees, outputs/table5_emp.csv lnchg_no_empl_mfg coef=-4.2305 x 1.06 = -4.48% vs paper -4.5%; (2) employment-to-population rate, outputs/table5_emp.csv net_empl_rate d_sh_empl coef=-0.7742 x 1.06 = -0.82 pp vs paper -0.8 pp; (3) mean log weekly earnings, outputs/table6_wage.csv d_avg_lnwkwage coef=-0.7592 x 1.06 = -0.80% vs paper -0.8%; (4) per-capita transfers, outputs/table8_trans.csv log_change coefs for disability (lnchg_trans_ssadis_pc=1.9597 -> 2.08%), income assistance (lnchg_trans_fedinc_pc=3.0391 -> 3.22%), and unemployment (lnchg_trans_unemp_pc=3.4599 -> 3.67%), spanning ~2.1 to 3.7% vs the paper's 2 to 3.5%. All four magnitudes reproduce within well under 5% of the paper values, and the transfer range brackets the reported 2-3.5%. fix_severity.json reports only one minor matplotlib-install fix with no impact on the statistical results, so the reproduced coefficients faithfully reflect the paper's method.
